name: How deep do you need to break the pool shell for permit approval?

mainEntity.name: How deep do you need to break the pool shell or open the bottom for permit approval in local cities?
mainEntity.text: How deep do you need to break the pool shell or open the bottom for permit approval in local cities?

acceptedAnswer.text: Permit approvals often depend on how the pool shell is opened before filling. Cities may require a breach in the bottom or a specified opening to improve drainage and help prevent water from collecting under the fill. The exact size and placement can vary, and some cities are more prescriptive than others. In the Los Angeles area, the requirements may depend on whether the pool is being fully demolished, partially removed, or simply abandoned and backfilled. Homeowners should not guess at the breach method, because the wrong approach can lead to failed inspection or future settlement issues. The contractor should match the opening method to the permit conditions and inspection checklist.
acceptedAnswer.description: Some jurisdictions require a hole or break in the pool bottom so the fill can drain and stabilize properly. The exact depth and size vary by city, permit conditions, and whether the pool is fully removed or filled in place.
